title: AI Email Drafting: Checks Before Anything Reaches a Subscriber
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: A model producing usable text is not authorization to send it. Define who approves the campaign, recipients, claims and delivery conditions. A failed check should leave the output as a draft, not trigger a less-restricted route.
content:
Keep generation separate from permission

A model producing usable text is not authorization to send it. Define who approves the campaign, recipients, claims and delivery conditions. A failed check should leave the output as a draft, not trigger a less-restricted route.

Use deterministic checks first

As an implementation pattern, validate required fields, unresolved personalization tokens, approved destinations and unsubscribe handling in code. These checks have a narrow purpose; they do not prove the rest of the copy is accurate or lawful.

Review the content, not only its score

A second model can assist review but can also miss the same error as the first. Human review is especially useful for new offers, sensitive claims and changes in audience. Keep an approved source for prices, policies and promises.

Test failures deliberately

Use synthetic recipients and a non-sending test environment to check timeouts, duplicate jobs, malformed output and denied approval. These are proposed safeguards, not a claim that every Laravel Mail installation already enforces them. Confirm the actual workflow before relying on it.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
